findings_summary: Independent adversarial review across three rounds of the follow-up that pins require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes to false so the tracked ruleset payload fully describes the live ruleset. The first review returned APPROVE_WITH_NITS (a GitHub App is installed org-wide, contradicting a 'no bot' claim); the second returned REQUEST_CHANGES with a HIGH finding that the repository DOES contain unattributed commits (47 of 319 on main, authored by an identity not linked to a GitHub account) — the opposite of what the revision claimed, and the very evidence that makes the parameter change necessary rather than merely prudent. The third review returned APPROVE with every factual claim reproduced and the payload blob unchanged. The decision itself was never in doubt: with no second eligible approver, the GitHub default can only deadlock, never protect.

findings.description: Justification text claimed 'no bot ... exists'; a GitHub App is installed org-wide holding contents:write (no commits produced).

Corrected text then claimed 'no commit or pull request is authored by a bot or an unattributed identity'. False: 47 of 319 commits on main (Issue Orchestrator <orchestrator@promptvault.dev>) are unattributed (author == null). This is the evidence justifying the false setting.
Internal contradiction: 'from an app token' was cited as an example of an unattributed commit while the correction asserted app-pushed commits carry attribution.
